3. After R1 finishes, reader R2 queries B, C, D. All still store (0, 0), so R2 returns 0.

With write-back, each reader queries three replicas, selects the highest-tagged pair, sends that exact pair to replicas, and waits for three processing acknowledgements before returning. A replica receiving an older tag keeps its newer pair; its acknowledgement still guarantees that its stored tag is at least the reader’s selected tag.

Here is the proof, including concurrent readers and unfinished writes:
• Every completed write or read leaves three replicas storing tags at least its own tag. Any later read queries three replicas, intersecting that completed operation’s quorum because 3 + 3 > 5. Since replica tags never decrease, the later read selects a tag at least as large. Thus completed reads cannot be followed by reads returning older tags, even if another reader concurrently writes back stale data.
• Every nonzero tag returned by a read originates from a writer operation. Reader write-back only copies existing tagged values; it creates none. If the originating write is unfinished, include it in the completed extension used for linearization. An unfinished write whose value is never returned can be omitted.
• Order included writes by their increasing tags. Place every read returning tag t after write t and before the next included write, ordering reads with equal tags consistently with real time. Reads returning tag zero precede the first write.
• This ordering respects real time. A completed write preceding a read forces the read’s tag to be at least that write’s tag through quorum intersection. A completed read preceding another read similarly forces nondecreasing tags. If a read finishes before a write starts, that new write’s tag is greater than the read’s tag, because tags increase and the read cannot observe a write that has not started. Writer-to-writer real-time order also agrees with increasing tags.

Each read therefore returns the value of the latest preceding write in this ordering. Concurrent readers may select different tags, and a read may expose an unfinished write, but neither breaks the proof: write-back preserves the quorum guarantee needed by subsequent operations.

rows.answer: The launch date is February 19, 2027. The replay must preserve that date because it was an explicit team decision tied to a signed customer deadline—not an estimate or an inferred date.

review.note: Final fixed-context probe preserves February 19, 2027 and explicit signed customer deadline rationale. Its frozen context is identical to the fresh-process control, distinct from growing natural meeting history.
